words.gloss: her elder sister (the Goddess of Misfortune)

literal: Having envied, him who has jealousy, the Goddess of Prosperity, her elder sister having shown, will leave.
translation: The Goddess of Prosperity will turn away from a person who harbors envy, and pointing him out to her elder sister, the Goddess of Misfortune, she will abandon him.
modern: பொறாமை கொண்டு அழுக்காறு உடையவனாக வாழ்பவனை, திருமகள் தன் மூத்தவளாகிய மூதேவிக்குக் காட்டிவிட்டு அவனிடமிருந்து நீங்கிவிடுவாள்.
explanation: This couplet warns against the destructive nature of envy by using the personified deities of wealth and poverty. The Goddess of Prosperity (Seyyavaḷ) cannot tolerate a person who harbors jealousy and grudges others' success. Instead of staying with such a person, she will point him out to her elder sister, the Goddess of Misfortune (Tavvai), and leave him in her hands. The contrast between 'Seyyavaḷ' and 'Tavvai' illustrates the complete reversal of fortune that awaits an envious person.
